plan: [ Second-price auction: bidding your true value is weakly dominant and maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding can make me win and pay above my value; underbidding can make me lose when winning would be profitable. Values are i.i.d. each round; no history advantage here. [ In a private-values, independent, second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This maximizes expected profit: you win exactly when your value is highest and pay the second-highest bid, avoiding the risk of paying more than your value. There is no prior-round information to adjust for. Values/bids allow 0.1 increments; 41.0 is valid. Therefore, I will bid my true value of 41 to maximize long-run profit. ]

[ In a second-price auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value.
